results.label: this tree ships the M112 trading-window rule (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
a desk with no window reports `unset` and says nothing is blocked on one — not an empty pass and not a guessed boundary
and it offers the suggestion as the trader’s own journal with nothing to derive yet, rather than a default window
the endpoint states its own limits: read-only, no writes, no permission granted, no prediction, no inferred window
and it carries the module’s basis and his own words, so the UI does not paraphrase the rule
no zone is owned yet, and the endpoint says so rather than assuming one
another trader’s window is not served: an unknown id and a FOREIGN trader’s account are both a 404, never an empty window
and neither can a foreign trader’s window be written
refuses a clock that is not HH:MM with its own code, at the status the app already uses for that class
refuses one side alone with its own code, at the status the app already uses for that class
refuses two equal sides with its own code, at the status the app already uses for that class
refuses a window before any zone is owned with its own code, at the status the app already uses for that class
refuses a window before any zone is owned, even with a zone supplied with its own code, at the status the app already uses for that class
and a refused write changes nothing: the desk still has no window after all five
the trader’s own zone is set through the account they already edit, and the window then has a clock to live on
an offset is refused once a zone IS owned: `+01:00` follows no daylight-saving rule, so it is not the trader’s own clock
a window the trader types is saved as `manual` and is NOT labelled as derived from the journal
and the saved window is evaluated immediately: outside its own hours the state is `outside` and it blocks
the trader may re-save a window, and the second save replaces the first without ever creating a second one
a window on a zone the desk does not own is refused, naming the zone it does own
and that refusal did not move the stored boundary either
before the routine is complete the entry is refused by the routine, so the window is not what stopped it yet
with the routine complete and the window outside, the entry is REFUSED by the window: 409, the guardrail code, and the window’s own rule in the breach list
and the refusal is the module sentence, naming the window, the zone and the local time there
no trade was written: a hard block refuses the entry rather than recording it as a mistake
and the permission the app answers with cannot be overridden from the client
the guardrails read is a 200 with the stop in it, not a 503: a blocked desk is a readable state, not a broken service
the SAME entry is admitted as soon as the clock is inside the window — the boundary, not the entry, is what refused it
clearing the window writes four NULLs and reports `unset` again — nothing is blocked on a window the trader removed
and an entry that arrives after the clear is admitted, which is what "blocks nothing" has to mean
the clear left no empty-window residue: all four columns are NULL, so an upgrade and a new desk look the same
an unrelated account edit (a rename, a cap change) cannot move a hard boundary: the window columns come back byte-identical
with 34 closed trades the desk now has a suggestion, labelled as the trader’s own recorded journal
the suggestion names the session, the count and the floor it cleared, rather than presenting a band as a finding
and the band is the middle of those entries’ own local hours, rounded outward to whole hours
the served suggestion IS the module’s computation over the same rows — the route adds no second derivation
a window the trader edits away from the candidate is recorded as `manual`, even with the suggestion available
accepting the suggestion stores exactly the candidate pair and records `from_session_history` — the trader accepted it, the app did not apply it
and a GET afterwards reports the same stored pair with its source, so the label survives the round trip
a desk with no owned zone cannot accept a suggestion either: the refusal says which fact is missing
below the 30-trade review floor the suggestion is WITHHELD, not presented as a smaller window
and accepting it is refused with the reason, so a below-floor band can never become the trader’s boundary by one click
a stored zone the runtime cannot resolve is reported as `unavailable` with the repair action — a 200 read, never a 500
and it BLOCKS the entry with its own rule: an unreadable window refuses rather than opening the gate
reading the broken window never repairs it behind the trader’s back: the stored row is exactly what was stored
an account edit cannot repair a window either: the boundary belongs to the window endpoint, so no unrelated write silently rewrites it
and the repair is the one the sentence named — re-saving the window in the owned zone — after which the state is readable and inside its hours again
changing the owned zone does NOT move the boundary: the window reports `unavailable` and names both clocks
so an entry cannot slip through on the new clock either — the same pair is refused until the trader re-saves it

scope: M112 api: the boundary over HTTP, and the entry it refuses: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
